summary: All seven full occurrences were checked. No new sense or stem is needed; three independent III Infectum contexts fill the cell to five.
III predicates restlessness of an unmarked experiencer/subject; bu fəkrano can mark the thought prompting it. No patient is required, and the III label does not entail causation.

II vollreden remains distinct from the III subject-state use. The supplied III 29/318 example has II-shaped mqaləq; preserve this inherited alternation as a morphological question rather than silently rewriting the stem.
The camel's movement and the fox's anxiety are participant/context extensions of restlessness. The edition's zitterte and bewegt sich do not establish two additional bodily-motion senses.
III Infectum-wa at 104/19 is a habitual reaction during chess instructions, not a semantically Detransitive event. Its entire relevant quotation is already inherited.
komalqat at 65/455 has a missing or contracted q relative to neighbouring komaqlaq. It is not published as a verified unusual form.
No new fixed phrase or light-verb collocation emerges. The II ear-patient phrase is already the inherited sole example and is not additional corpus evidence here.
At 65/455 is komalqat a genuine contraction of maqləq/maqlaq or an omitted q in the edition? Verify before adding a form example.
What is the exact meaning and segmentation of qm i ruḥo at PrS 74/51, and is maqəlqo a regular feminine realization of maqləq?
Does III mqaləq at 29/318 reflect stem variation, dialect phonology or source transcription? Keep it with the inherited III example until resolved.
Does PrS 71/112 describe actual bodily trembling or only agitation? German zitterte alone was not used to create a sense.
Restore the missing subject and correct the pronoun after nach.
before: wenn aber seine Hand nach sie (einer Figur) ausstreckte
after: wenn er aber seine Hand nach ihr (einer Figur) ausstreckte
rationale: The German clause requires the subject er; seine Hand is the object of ausstreckte. The pronoun referring to einer Figur must be dative ihr after nach. The supplied 104/19 translation confirms the action, although it too omits er.

summary: Animal restlessness and bodily stirring are contextual realizations of unruhig werden, alongside mental agitation and the inherited chess reaction; German zitterte alone does not establish a trembling sense.
